output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. The audit trail shows about 37 and 36 cases a month were confirmed as incidents in Sep and Oct, in line with the earlier ~38 a month. 47 of those cases were then moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring". Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, while the case carried the SLA-warning flag and had no containment recorded. A script on a Brackwater analyst jump host, using the integration account, made every one of those changes. It checked for flagged cases about every 5 minutes and re-categorised each one within minutes. That looks deliberate, not a platform fault. It also removes the slow cases from the containment-time and SLA figures, so the 100% SLA result and the bonus claim are unreliable. The Suspicious Activity queue growth fits this. Do not cut the Halvard retainer and do not pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have your own team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Get Brackwater's written account and review the contract position, including the service credits, before the renewal. I haven't checked whether the 28 dropped detection rules left real gaps. Review that separately.
